pure-announcement.rationale: It is a practitioner essay arguing for an instrumentation model, with no product launch, release, or funding content anywhere in it.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts (Cypher querying, retrieval composition, MCP notes, SIEM gap) contain nothing about wide events or the metrics/logs/traces pillar model.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The central claim is a checkable mapping — spans are wide events with SpanId/TraceId/ParentSpanId, metrics are periodic snapshot events — stated against quoted, linked OpenTelemetry docs and the documented Scuba system.

durability.rationale: The argument that logs, metrics, and traces are projections of high-cardinality wide events is a data-model position with no version numbers or vendor matrices, and it has only gained relevance as the 'observability 2.0' debate since 2024.

actionability.rationale: It changes how a reader instruments: emit one context-rich event per unit of work without cardinality fear, carry the sampling rate in-band and aggregate with SUM(samplingRate), and pick tooling on raw-event slice-and-dice rather than pre-aggregation.

atomicity.rationale: One idea carries the whole piece — wide events subsume the three pillars — and the sampling and explorable-UI material are facets of that same idea rather than separable concepts.
